newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom lifts Q3 pretax profits.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom lifts Q3 pretax profits.

text.p: British Telecommuncations Plc posted higher third quarter pretax profits on Thursday and said demand for its range and quality of telephony products remained at a healthy level.
Third quarter pretax profits rose to 909 million pounds ($1.46 billion) after a 39 million pound redundancy charge, up from 829 million pounds in the third quarter in the previous financial year.
"We look forward with confidence to a satisfactory outcome for the full year," BT chairman Sir Iain Vallance said in a statement.
Analysts had pencilled in pretax profits in a range of 860-920 million pounds.

Profit before taxation for the nine months came in at 2.51 million pounds, 73 million pounds higher than the corresponding period the previous year. The results were hit by higher redundancy charges and a 60 million pound premium on the repurchase of government-held bonds.

BT, which hopes to seal a $20 billion merger with America's MCI Communications in the autumn, said sales rose 4.3 percent in the nine months to December 31, 1996, helped by the group's expanding overseas operations, telephone exchange line rentals and mobile communications.
Mobile phone turnover grew by 11.7 percent in the nine months, reflecting the 16.7 percent growth in BT's majority-owned Cellnet unit's customer base in the year.
Cellnet had 2.7 million customer connections at the period end of which over 880,000 were digital.
